[PAPER_0063, relevance_score=0.222] As noted previously, this manipulation was found to enhance all of the facets of meaning in life in a previous data set (Edwards, 2024).

However, in this case, it did not affect meaning in life or its facets. One possible explanation for this failure is that Study 6 data were collected in temporal proximity to hurricane season in the United States and the notion that climate change is hopeless may have been more believable than the notion that there is still hope.

[PAPER_0064, relevance_score=0.194] In any case, it is important to bear in mind that mediation analyses in Study 6 suggest that to the extent that the manipulations induced feelings of hopefulness (vs. hopelessness) did relate positively to global meaning in life and purpose. In this regard, a potential explanation for these findings may be that hopeful people, at a dispositional level, experience greater meaning.

Additionally, one reason induced hope did not directly affect meaning in life as predicted may be a lack of ecologically validity.

[PAPER_0068, relevance_score=0.199] All studies were conducted online. Certainly, continuing to develop manipulations of hopeful feelings is an important goal for research. Moreover, how hope inductions may be beneficial in clinical interventions, and for whom, warrants future research.
